chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of his companions, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Jameela, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a slave and a free man who both killed a free man, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If he (the guardian of the deceased) so desires, he can kill the free one, and if he so desires, he can kill the slave. So if he were to choose to kill the free one, he should whip the side of the slave.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a slave and a free man jointly kill a free man?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the juristic option (khiyar) granted to the victim's heir in cases of joint homicide by a slave and a free man, reflecting the classical Shia view on the differential status of slaves in retribution. It highlights the practical application of qisas, where choosing to execute the free man results in the slave receiving flogging rather than death, underscoring the distinct legal weight assigned to freedom in Islamic penal code.
